data.body:
BOTH CHILDREN CLOSED — this parent's work is complete.

  S1 [rebar:f2f3-9cb1-335b-4e31] — CLOSED. Gerrit 1179, main 529e802da0. The retry/error cluster
    relocated out of `transport.py` into `adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py`, byte-identically
    (789 -> 683 lines; retry.py 162). Forced by the locked 800-line cap, which left eleven lines
    of headroom and made S2 unwritable in place.
  S2 [rebar:6758-26b8-c9ea-4c5d] — CLOSED. Gerrit 1185 (+ 1190 for the number provenance),
    main ddf0a0af9. `Retry-After` honoured on 429, scoped to IDEMPOTENT READS via a per-call
    opt-in that DEFAULTS TO OFF.

THE SPLIT WAS VINDICATED, and that is the durable lesson from this ticket. b586 hit BLOCK on ten
consecutive plan-review rounds as a single story. Split into a mechanical relocation and a policy
change, S1 PASSED FIRST TRY and this parent then PASSED WITH ZERO BLOCKING FINDINGS. Same move as
J9 -> J10 earlier in this epic: when a plan keeps returning double-digit findings, suspect
STRUCTURE rather than wording — it was carrying two independent changes, and every fix to one
re-opened the other.

The two hazards this parent's rounds identified were both real and both survived into the
implementation as constraints:
 1. NO THIRD `Retry-After` IMPLEMENTATION. `_errors.parse_retry_after` and `MAX_BACKOFF_S` are
    reused; `dispatch_one.py:148-172` was already a 429 path. Only the delay ARITHMETIC diverges
    (Atlassian prescribes jitter on the DC bucket; that path applies none), and the divergence is
    stated in the code rather than left to look like a slip.
 2. IT WOULD HAVE REINTRODUCED THE DUPLICATE-ISSUE CLASS 21fc JUST FIXED. `_with_connection_retry`
    is the choke point for ALL transport calls including `create_issue`, and a 429 can arrive
    AFTER the server began a write. Hence opt-in, defaulting OFF, so a mutation added later cannot
    inherit the retry by omission — asserted per member over an explicit enumeration of the ten
    mutating transport members.

S2's review also found a design gap worth recording here: the opt-in has to reach the retry layer
by TWO paths, not one. `get_comment_map` fetches comments one request PER ISSUE through a DIRECT
`_with_connection_retry` call that bypasses `_call_logged` entirely — the highest-volume read in a
pass, and therefore the likeliest to trip a token bucket, was exactly the call the single-path
design could not reach.
